minutes.headline: Water Commissioners voted to deny Kevin O'Brien's request to extend water service for a private water company.
minutes.summary: The board reviewed minutes, then took up Kevin O'Brien's attorney opinion and voted to deny extending service to his property for creating a private water company selling water outside the district. The superintendent reported on PFAS pilot testing, an access/parking problem at the pilot site, and the MassDOT permit for the water main replacement. Public comment centered on the state revolving fund loan approval and plans for a spring special meeting vote.

public_comment.topic: Said the board's vote on Mr. O'Brien's request should be recorded in the minutes as a response, and supported signs saying no parking to keep 24/7 access.
Asked about the state revolving fund (SRF) funding the district was approved for and what it means.
Asked whether the state will eventually force PFAS treatment at greater cost; discussion of timing and rates.
Commended the board for educating the public on PFAS and pursuing funding.

votes.motion: Deny Mr. O'Brien's request to extend service to his property and sell water for creation of a water company selling inside and outside the district (restated motion, seconded)

budget_items.what_was_said: A figure for a full-blown pilot test was mentioned, with hope of shortening the timeframe.
Commissioners noted the project estimate versus bid and award, with contingency and borrowing; they discussed pipe cost increases.

budget_items.topic: ARPA funds for Kings well pilot study
budget_items.what_was_said: ARPA money is funding the pilot study for the Kings well.
The district was approved for a zero-interest SRF loan with possible principal forgiveness, requiring voter approval by June 2024.
A commercial bond rate was compared unfavorably with the SRF loan; Littleton's loan and forgiveness were cited.

decisions.decision: No motion on the pilot site access issue; board will communicate with the property management company about signage and 24/7 access.
Water district plans to hold its regular annual meeting and a special meeting around May with one article for the SRF loan borrowing (two-thirds vote).

what_happened.line: The Water Commissioners voted to deny Kevin O'Brien's request to extend district service to his property for a private water company selling water inside and outside the district.
The superintendent reported on PFAS pilot testing, including an access and parking problem at the pilot site; no motion was made and the board will contact the property management company.
Commissioners discussed the MassDOT permit and water main replacement, comparing the project estimate with the bid and award, and noted contingency and pipe cost increases.
Residents heard that the district was approved for a zero-interest state revolving fund loan, with possible principal forgiveness, that requires voter approval by June 2024.
The district plans a regular annual meeting and a special meeting around May, with one article for the loan borrowing, which needs a two-thirds vote.

why_it_matters: Residents of the district will be asked to vote on borrowing for the water main and PFAS work, and a two-thirds vote is needed for the zero-interest loan, which may include principal forgiveness, to proceed.
The denial sets a position on whether district water can be extended to supply a separate private water company outside the district.
